original_question: Let f and g be superattracting germs in End(C^n,O) with c(f)=c(g). Is local conjugacy equivalent to conjugacy of postcritical sets: topological conjugacy iff a local homeomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g), and holomorphic conjugacy iff a local biholomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g)?
target_in_paper: Theorem 0.3 (Local Böttcher Coordinates), with the broader motivation supplied by the classification question in Section 4; the paper does not formulate a pairwise f-versus-g conjecture in terms of postcritical-set equivalence.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main local-dynamical ingredients the paper cares about: higher-dimensional superattracting germs, local conjugacy near the fixed point, and the postcritical set as the geometric object that controls whether a germ should behave like its model map. It also points in the same direction as the paper’s later classification question in Section 4.
missing_details: The paper’s exact local statement is not about two arbitrary germs f and g with c(f)=c(g); it is about one germ F and its quasihomogeneous part H.
The ambient space is a complex vector space E of dimension m, decomposed as E = E1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Ep, not just C^n with a single order parameter c(f).
The relevant model map is quasihomogeneous: H = H1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Hp, where each Hj:Ej→Ej is homogeneous of degree kj ≥ 2 and nondegenerate, meaning Hj^{-1}(0) = {0}.
The paper requires F to have an adapted superattracting fixed point: Fj(v) = Hj(vj) + O(∥v∥∥vj∥^{kj}) as v→0 for every j.
The conjugacy in the theorem is holomorphic/analytic only, and it is normalized by Φ(0)=0 and D0Φ=id.
Your draft adds a topological classification statement, but the paper does not prove such a theorem; topological classification is only raised as a later open-ended question.
The paper does not use a bare condition that a homeomorphism or biholomorphism sends PCrit(f) onto PCrit(g) as the criterion.
Instead, the postcritical condition is formulated through admissible vector fields tangent to the postcritical set.

An admissible p-tuple must be specified: each vector field is analytic near 0, tangent to Ej, vanishes on E′j = {vj=0}, satisfies ζj(v)=ϑj(v)+o(∥v∥) with ϑj(v)=(v;vj), and all fields commute pairwise.
The phrase 'postcritical set' is used in the theorem via tangency to the critical value set of F^n for every n ≥ 1 in some sufficiently small neighborhood U where F:U→F(U)⊆U is proper.
The paper’s equivalent dynamical formulation DF ∘ ξj = kj · ξj ∘ F near 0 is omitted in your draft.
The equality c(f)=c(g) in your draft is not the paper’s invariant; the paper uses the full multidegree (k1,…,kp).
The theorem does not compare arbitrary local biholomorphisms/homeomorphisms between postcritical sets; it compares F to its fixed quasihomogeneous model H.

If one wants to connect your draft to the paper’s broader intent, one must say explicitly that the paper only asks later whether a topological and/or analytic classification of higher-dimensional superattracting germs exists and whether the two coincide.
refined_question: Let E be a complex vector space decomposed as E = E1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Ep, and let F:(E,0)→(E,0) be an analytic germ with an adapted superattracting fixed point, meaning that for each j there is a nondegenerate homogeneous map Hj:Ej→Ej of degree kj ≥ 2 such that Fj(v)=Hj(vj)+O(∥v∥∥vj∥^{kj}) as v→0; write H = H1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ Hp for the quasihomogeneous part of F. Is F locally biholomorphically conjugate to H by a germ Φ with Φ(0)=0 and D0Φ=id if and only if there exists an admissible p-tuple of analytic vector field germs (ζ1,…,ζp), where each ζj is tangent to Ej, vanishes on E′j={vj=0}, satisfies ζj(v)=ϑj(v)+o(∥v∥) with ϑj(v)=(v;vj), the fields commute pairwise, and each ζj is tangent, on some sufficiently small neighborhood U on which F:U→F(U)⊆U is proper, to the critical value set of F^n:U→F^n(U) for every n ≥ 1?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as proved in the paper, one may replace the postcritical-tangency condition by: there exists an admissible p-tuple of analytic vector field germs (ξ1,…,ξp) such that DF ∘ ξj = kj · ξj ∘ F near 0 for every j.
justification: The draft is trying to turn the paper’s postcritical-set philosophy into a classification principle. But the nearest exact official formulation in the inspected paper is Theorem 0.3, not a pairwise f-versus-g conjecture. The introduction explains that the postcritical geometry must look like an analytic cone if a germ is to be locally conjugate to a homogeneous model, and Theorem 0.3 makes this precise for analytic conjugacy to the quasihomogeneous part H by using admissible vector fields tangent to the postcritical set. The only broader classification statement in the paper appears later as a general question asking whether one can give topological and/or analytic classifications of higher-dimensional superattracting germs and whether they coincide. So your draft is directionally right, but it is broader than the paper’s exact theorem and sharper than the paper’s explicit open question, while missing the paper’s indispensable setup and the precise vector-field formulation.
